detail.evidence:
MECHANISM: CONFIRMED (traced + executed). CONSEQUENCE: REFUTED — the S1 impact ("we follow a chain the rest of the network will not", "Core peers rejected the block we accepted") is not reachable.

Core side is exactly as claimed. refs/bitcoin/src/primitives/transaction.h:222-231 — after reading the per-vin stacks, `if (!tx.HasWitness()) throw std::ios_base::failure("Superfluous witness record");`. And it is on the live wire paths: refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:4866 `vRecv >> TX_WITH_WITNESS(*pblock);` and :4486 `vRecv >> TX_WITH_WITNESS(ptx);` (allow_witness=true), so the message genuinely fails to deserialize. Even the RPC path refuses it: refs/bitcoin/src/core_io.cpp:171-224 DecodeTx tries TX_WITH_WITNESS (throws), then TX_NO_WITNESS, which reads the 0x00 dummy as an empty vin and then misparses — neither decode consumes the input.

Our side is also as claimed, and there is no guard anywhere else. src/serialization/types.lisp:209-232 (br-read-transaction) and :266-289 (read-transaction) check only `(unless (= flag 1) ...)` and never test emptiness; parse-tx-payload (src/serialization/messages.lisp:441-457) only rejects trailing bytes; parse-block-payload (:519-525) is a bare br-read-bitcoin-block; %check-block (src/validation/block.lisp:1583-1687) has no encoding-canonicality check (its weight and legacy-size checks are computed from the PARSED form via calculate-block-weight / serialize-transaction). `grep -rn "Superfluous" src/` hits only serialize-side comments (types.lisp:422, rpc/mining.lisp:52).

EXECUTED (warm image, exit 0):
  (bl.ser:parse-tx-payload <version|00|01|1 vin|1 vout|00|locktime>)
  => (:PARSED T :HAS-WITNESS NIL :WITNESS #(NIL)
      :TXID "ead046e6...426dfe05" :WTXID "ead046e6...426dfe05"
      :REWIRE "0200000001c1e1...bd600000000")   ; legacy, marker/flag gone
  Block level: a 166-byte block payload carrying that tx and a 163-byte payload
  carrying its canonical twin parse to the SAME block hash
  (4b5f23b2...a15e9f11), SAME txid, SAME weight (652).

WHY THE IMPACT DOES NOT FOLLOW. The superfluous encoding is semantically identical to the canonical one, and every artifact we derive or emit is the canonical form:
 - store-block persists `(bl.ser:serialize-witness-block block)` (src/storage/blocks.lisp:385-387), and serialize-witness-block emits the marker/flag only when transaction-has-witness-p (src/serialization/types.lisp:577-589) — which is NIL here.
 - handle-getdata serves blocks by re-serializing from the store via make-block-message (src/networking/protocol.lisp:2116-2133); make-tx-message uses transaction-wire-bytes / serialize-transaction (src/serialization/messages.lisp:421-429).
 EXECUTED: parse the 166-byte superfluous block, then serialize-witness-block it → :RESERIALIZED-EQUALS-CANONICAL T, length 163, and the make-block-message payload is byte-identical to the canonical block. So a Core peer that fetches the block from us receives bytes it parses and accepts; the block's content, txids, wtxids, merkle root, weight and header hash are unchanged. There is no chain the network cannot follow — we hand it a parseable copy of the same block, and the attacker gains nothing over simply sending the canonical encoding. The mempool half is likewise inert: we re-encode canonically on relay, so peers see an ordinary tx.

WHAT SURVIVES (S3): a real parser-strictness divergence — our deserializer accepts a non-canonical BIP144 encoding that Core rejects by design, and silently normalizes it. No consensus, chain-state, DoS or relay consequence is reachable today (the only measurable effect is ≤2 extra bytes per witnessless tx on an inbound message, still bounded by the message-size cap). It is worth closing as defense-in-depth — the tree's own fuzz docstring (tests/fuzz-property-tests.lisp:150-162) names "accepts a non-canonical encoding and then normalises it" as the shape that has split other implementations — but it is not S1.

MECHANISM: granted. refs/bitcoin/src/primitives/transaction.h:229-231 throws "Superfluous witness record" when (flags&1) and !tx.HasWitness(); our br-read-transaction (src/serialization/types.lisp:209-232) and read-transaction (:266-289) have no such guard. Executed in the warm image:

  (parse-tx-payload "0100000000010100...00ffffffff0100000000000000 00 00 00000000")
  => (:PARSED T :HAS-WITNESS NIL :WITNESS-SLOT #(NIL)
      :TXID "89d3fe04e0abfd5038d4c26d8935e3feff1122b429c5f8fb4efb74d12f4de73d"
      :WIRE "01000000010000...ffffffff0100000000000000000000000000"  ; LEGACY form
      :WEIGHT 240)

We accept bytes Core refuses. That much stands.

CONSEQUENCE: refuted. The stated impact ("a block whose bytes every Core node rejects while we accept and build on it... we follow a chain the rest of the network will not") does not follow, because the parse is normalising and nothing downstream ever re-emits the hostile bytes. Executed proof — I built the same 1-tx block in both encodings and round-tripped each through br-read-bitcoin-block:

  :RESER-EQUAL T                 ; serialize-witness-block(ext) == serialize-witness-block(legacy)
  :RESER-IS-LEGACY-INPUT T       ; and it is byte-identical to the canonical legacy block
  :BLOCKHASH1 == :BLOCKHASH2 = 4be7570e8f70eb093640c8468274ba759745a7aa2b7d25ab1e0421b259845014
  :TXID1 == :TXID2 = 89d3fe04e0abfd5038d4c26d8935e3feff1122b429c5f8fb4efb74d12f4de73d

So the block we accept IS the block Core accepts: same hash, same tx set, and its canonical serialization is a block Core parses and validates normally. There is no block that we accept and Core rejects on consensus grounds — only a byte string Core cannot parse, which we never reproduce. Core's block-message deserialize failure is caught in ProcessMessages and does not mark the hash invalid, so Core simply picks the block up from any honest peer (including us) in canonical form. No split, transient or permanent.

Every re-emission path normalises, traced individually:
- disk: store-block (src/storage/blocks.lisp:366-387) writes (bl.ser:serialize-witness-block block), and serialize-witness-block (types.lisp:578-590) emits the marker/flag pair only when transaction-has-witness-p — which is NIL here. So the non-canonical encoding does NOT enter the block store (this also corrects docs/gap-analysis-9.md:367, which claimed it does).
- block relay: src/serialization/messages.lisp:438 -> serialize-witness-block, same normalisation. handle-block (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1060-1069) parses to a struct; no raw payload is ever forwarded.
- tx relay: messages.lisp:427 -> transaction-wire-bytes (types.lisp:416-425), which explicitly branches on transaction-has-witness-p precisely to avoid emitting a form Core would reject; its docstring names "Superfluous witness record".
- mempool accounting: mempool.lisp:253 sizes entries with transaction-wire-bytes, i.e. the legacy size Core computes — so not even a size-accounting skew. The wire inflation is 2 + n_inputs bytes (~2% at best) and is bounded by the 4 MB message cap anyway.

"Lets a peer put into our mempool a transaction Core cannot parse at all" is also wrong: the resulting mempool entry is exactly the legacy transaction Core parses, with the same txid and wtxid (wtxid == txid when has-witness is NIL), and we relay it in that form. The attacker gains nothing they could not get by sending the legacy encoding.

Mixed stacks are not an escape hatch: transaction-has-witness-p (types.lisp:169-173) is `some non-null`, matching Core's HasWitness() (`any !scriptWitness.IsNull()`), so any tx with a real witness item takes the witness path in both trees.

No consensus split, no fund loss, no remote crash or DoS a peer can trigger. What remains is a parser-strictness divergence: sendrawtransaction/decoderawtransaction/submitblock accept hex Core rejects, and a differential fuzzer against Core would diverge. That is the same family as the trailing-bytes case already guarded in parse-tx-payload (messages.lisp:441-457) — worth fixing, but S3.

Independently corroborated: this identical finding was already adjudicated in this repo today — docs/gap-analysis-10.md:60 records "mechanism confirmed, impact refuted — S3 (was S1)", and docs/gap-analysis-9.md:367 filed it under S3 as "contained (txids and weights are unaffected)". It is a re-raise of a settled item, and my execution above reproduces that verdict from scratch.

s2.evidence:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION. Grep over src/ and tests/ finds *LAST-CHECKSIG-ERROR* (src/coalton/interop.lisp:2207) and *LAST-CHECKMULTISIG-ERROR* (interop.lisp:2323) only in DEFVAR and SETF positions — no LET/PROGV binding anywhere, so every write hits the global symbol-value. Compare validate-tx-scripts (src/validation/block.lisp:806-810), which DOES let-bind bl.interop:*script-flags*, *precomputed-sighash* and *current-spent-utxos* (thread-local per worker) but not these two; %script-check-worker (block.lisp:875-920) binds nothing either.
Ran (warm image): `(setf sym :sig-der)` in the main thread, a bt:make-thread setting it NIL, join → `(:AFTER-OTHER-THREAD-RESET NIL :BOUND-P T)`.
Then the real API: main thread with *script-flags*="STRICTENC,DERSIG" called VERIFY-CHECKSIG-FOR-SCRIPT on a malformed sig → error recorded; a second thread then ran VERIFY-CHECKSIG-FOR-SCRIPT with flags off; result → `(:A-ERR-BEFORE :SIG-DER :A-HAD-BEFORE T :A-HAD-AFTER-B NIL :GLOBAL-AFTER NIL)`. The other thread's entry-time `(setf *last-checksig-error* nil)` (interop.lisp:2214) erased the first thread's verdict, so LAST-CHECKSIG-HAD-STRICTENC-ERROR-P now answers NIL where it must answer T. That reader is exactly what the Coalton OP_CHECKSIG handler consults (src/coalton/script.lisp:1904-1909: `(if strictenc-error (ScriptErr SE-VerifyFailed) (ScriptOk ...push true/false...))`), and it overrides even a successful verify — so the reverse direction turns a VALID CHECKSIG into SE-VerifyFailed. Core's shape is per-invocation `ScriptError* serror` (refs/bitcoin/src/script/interpreter.cpp EvalChecksigPreTapscript), confirming the divergence.
CONSEQUENCE, scoped: only the pool path races. bl:*parallel-block-validation* is NIL by default (src/config.lisp:106) and is turned on only by -par=N>1 (src/config-options.lisp:355-360, a supported Core-compatible option). At default settings script execution is serialized by the single recursive node-lock — the sync thread holds it around message handlers and RPC handlers take it around validation (src/rpc/accessors.lisp:1-35; testmempoolaccept wraps validate-transaction-for-mempool in with-node-lock, src/rpc/mempool.lisp:539-560) — so I found no default-config concurrency for these globals. Nothing in the code documents this race: the *parallel-block-validation* docstring lists only the (fixed) coins-view cache race and the (open) libsecp alien-cache crash. Real, silent, non-deterministic, consensus-visible when -par>1; S2 stands.

s2.title_prefix: Lax (pre-BIP66) DER signature parser diverges from Core's ec
s2.evidence:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, IMPACT OVERSTATED. src/crypto/secp256k1.lisp:435-437 reads the R/S INTEGER length as a plain byte with no `& 0x80` long-form branch, and normalize-signature-lax (secp256k1.lisp:487-489) funnels the bignum through integer-to-bytes-be with byte-count 32 (secp256k1.lisp:454-460), which masks rather than fails. Core's ecdsa_signature_parse_der_lax handles long form for R (refs/bitcoin/src/pubkey.cpp:84-106) and S (119-145) and sets `overflow = 1` → all-zero signature when rlen/slen > 32 after stripping zeros (pubkey.cpp:157-171).
Ran both vectors against a real signature (privkey=0x01*32, msg=0x07*32, sig 3043021f1af7…):
  A. long-form R length `3044 02 81 1f <r31> 02 20 <s>` → :A-NORMALIZE NIL, :A-VERIFY-LAX (NIL T). Core parses rlen=0x1f and verifies TRUE. We say false, Core says true.
  B. inflated R `3045 02 21 01 00 <r31> 02 20 <s>` (= 2^256+r) → our normalize returns r||s ("001af75f…f74d") and :B-VERIFY-LAX (T T). Core: rlen=33, no leading zero, overflow → zero sig → FALSE. We say true, Core says false.
So the two-way divergence is real and the lax path is live: verify-signature uses normalize-signature-lax whenever :strict is NIL (secp256k1.lisp:855-865), and verify-checksig sets strict-der = DERSIG or STRICTENC or LOW_S (src/coalton/interop.lisp:2063-2065), all three off only below the BIP66 gate (src/validation/block.lisp:322-323).
WHERE THE FILING IS WRONG: (1) "Reachable on regtest below height 1351" is false for BOTH trees — Core d3056bc sets regtest consensus.BIP66Height = 1 (refs/bitcoin/src/kernel/chainparams.cpp:571, "Always active unless overridden"), as do signet (330) and testnet4 (482); our chainparams match (src/util/chainparams.lisp:214/250/285 all :bip66-height 1). Only mainnet <363,725 and testnet3 <330,776 leave DERSIG off. (2) The "IBD stalls permanently" consequence does not occur under default config: pre-BIP66 heights are far below the assumevalid block, and signature checks there are SKIPPED (src/networking/ibd.lisp:622-656 assumevalid-skip-height / script-checks-skippable-p, mirroring Core fScriptChecks), so the parser is never reached unless the operator sets -assumevalid=0. (3) No new pre-BIP66 block can be mined on any live chain, so direction (b) cannot be exercised by an attacker at the tip; mempool/relay always runs STANDARD flags (DERSIG on, block.lisp:270-286). Genuine consensus-code divergence worth fixing, but with no reachable relay/sync/wallet/resource consequence under any default configuration → S3, not S2.

s2.title_prefix: Fee estimator has no `validForFeeEstimation` gate: it track
s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED, traced and executed.

Core side verified verbatim at refs/bitcoin/src/policy/fees/block_policy_estimator.cpp:596-636 — `if (txHeight != nBestSeenHeight) return;` (:607) then `const bool validForFeeEstimation = !tx.m_mempool_limit_bypassed && !tx.m_submitted_in_package && tx.m_chainstate_is_current && tx.m_has_no_mempool_parents;` (:619) with `if (!validForFeeEstimation) { untrackedTxs++; return; }`. The four flags are supplied at refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:1305-1308 (`NewMempoolTransactionInfo(..., args.m_bypass_limits, args.m_package_submission, IsCurrentForFeeEstimation(m_active_chainstate), m_pool.HasNoInputsOf(tx))`), field docs at refs/bitcoin/src/kernel/mempool_entry.h:173-199.

Our side: src/mempool/mempool.lisp:866-871 — accept-validated-tx calls `(bpe-note-entry txid (mempool-entry-fee entry) (mempool-entry-vsize entry) height)` under nothing but `(when (eq result :ok) ...)`. src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:352-362 (bpe-process-transaction) filters on `(unless (gethash txid tracked) ...)` only — no height comparison against block-policy-estimator-best-height, no bypass/package/parents/chainstate flag. src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:554-561 (bpe-note-entry) adds only `(plusp vsize)`.

Absence verified by grep, not assumed: `grep -rn "current-for-fee|valid-for-fee|validForFeeEstimation|has-no-mempool-parents|best-seen-height|untracked" src/` returns ZERO hits. `grep -rn bpe-note-entry src/` returns exactly one call site (mempool.lisp:871) plus the definition and the export — so the check has not moved elsewhere.

All four excluded classes reach that one call site: reorg re-add src/validation/block.lisp:2894 (validate with `:bypass-limits t`, then accept-validated-tx `:defer-trim t`); package submission src/validation/packages.lisp:218 (%accept-into-mempool, `:defer-trim t`); mempool.dat reload src/node/mempool-persist.lisp:111; and the orphan cascade src/networking/protocol.lisp:1495, which by construction admits transactions WITH an in-mempool parent — exactly Core's HasNoInputsOf exclusion.

EXECUTED (scripts/dev.sh eval): estimator with best-height 800000, two entries noted at heights 700000 and 12345 →
  (:TRACKED-COUNT 2 :ENTRIES ((#(1 2 3) (700000 50000.0d0)) (#(4 5 6) (12345 2500.0d0))))
Core returns at :607 for both. Ours buckets both into all three horizons.

Consequence is reachable: src/node/init.lisp:759 installs *block-policy-estimator* at startup; src/mempool/fee-estimator.lisp:349-353 makes bpe-smart-fee-sat-per-vb the FIRST answer of estimate-fee-rate, which src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:212 (estimatesmartfee) consumes, and bpe-estimate-raw-fee backs estimaterawfee (rawtransaction.lisp:928). Partial mitigation only: rawtransaction.lisp:209 suppresses a feerate while `rpc-is-syncing`, so the "node behind" narrative is blunted at the reporting boundary — but the contaminated samples persist in the long horizon (one-week half-life) after sync completes, and the chained-child/reorg/package contamination is unaffected by that guard. Severity stays S2: real, systematic, wallet-money-affecting bias; no consensus effect.

s2.title_prefix: We never push an unsolicited cmpctblock to peers that sele
s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED, traced and executed.

Core side verified: refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:2144-2152 (NewPoWValidBlock) — `if (state.m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks && !PeerHasHeader(&state, pindex) && PeerHasHeader(&state, pindex->pprev)) { ... PushMessage(*pnode, ser_cmpctblock.Copy()); }`; and :5893-5910 (SendMessages) — `if (vHeaders.size() == 1 && state.m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks)` pushes m_most_recent_compact_block (or re-reads the block) instead of the headers announcement. `m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks` is set from the peer's sendcmpct at :3918 alongside `m_bip152_highbandwidth_from` at :3921 — i.e. it is exactly "the peer selected US".

Our side: src/networking/protocol.lisp:3053-3072 (relay-block) builds only `make-headers-message` and `make-inv-message` and branches solely on `peer-prefers-headers`. It is our ONLY unsolicited block announcement: `grep -rn relay-block src/` gives the definition, one caller in the block handler (protocol.lisp:1088) and one in submitblock/mining (src/rpc/mining.lisp:511); the only other block-carrying sends (protocol.lisp:2379 getheaders response, :2405 getblocks response) are replies to requests.

Not moved elsewhere: `grep -rn "cmpctblock|make-cmpctblock-message" src/` yields exactly two send sites — HANDLE-GETDATA's MSG_CMPCT_BLOCK responder (protocol.lisp:2131-2132, which does reuse the cache via bl.val:most-recent-cmpctblock) and the message constructor. `grep -rn "peer-compact-block-high-bandwidth\b" src/` → set at protocol.lisp:3260 (handle-sendcmpct), read ONLY at src/rpc/net.lisp:247 for getpeerinfo's bip152_hb_from. No code path reads it to drive a send.

EXECUTED (scripts/dev.sh eval, sb-int:encapsulate probe on send-message, peer with compact-block-high-bandwidth = T, version 2, state :ready):
  (:HB-FROM-PEER T :SENT-COMMANDS ("inv"))
and with prefers-headers also T:
  (:HB-AND-SENDHEADERS ("headers"))
Never "cmpctblock".

Consequence reachable: Core promotes to HB whichever peer sourced the block first (net_processing.cpp:2216-2222 → MaybeSetPeerAsAnnouncingHeaderAndIDs, :1273), regardless of whether the block arrived compact or full — so our node genuinely gets selected, then never honours the push, costing that peer a getdata round trip per block. Two small overstatements in the filing, not enough to refute: (a) the cache is not "wasted", it is used by the getdata responder at protocol.lisp:2131; (b) getpeerinfo's `bip152_hb_from` is a faithful report of the peer's request (same semantics as Core's m_bip152_highbandwidth_from), not a false advertisement of our behaviour. Severity stays S2: relay latency, no functional or consensus loss (the block still propagates one RTT later).

Incidental (out of scope, noted): our handle-sendcmpct (protocol.lisp:3256-3260) only ever SETS the flag on hb=true and never clears it on hb=false, where Core assigns both ways (`nodestate->m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks = sendcmpct_hb;`, :3918).

MECHANISM (partly confirmed, one of four items wrong). Core: refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:4161-4216 ContextualCheckBlock takes only pindexPrev and runs IsFinalTx / BIP34 height / CheckWitnessMalleation / GetBlockWeight, called at validation.cpp:4383 before SaveBlockToDisk, failure -> InvalidBlockFound (BLOCK_FAILED_VALID). Ours: src/validation/block.lisp:1916-1917 validate-block returns T for :context-free-only right after %check-block; finality (block.lisp:1828-1829 :non-final-tx), BIP34 (validate-coinbase-height, ~block.lisp:1860) and witness malleation (validate-witness-commitment, ~block.lisp:1848) all sit in %contextual-check-block, which src/networking/protocol.lisp:1023-1029 reaches only for tip-extending blocks.

RAN (dev.sh eval, regtest fixture): mined a regtest block, then set its coinbase witness to a 4-byte item (what Core rejects as CheckWitnessMalleation/bad-witness-nonce-size) ->
  (:FULL-BEFORE (T NIL) :FULL-AFTER (NIL :BAD-WITNESS-NONCE-SIZE) :CONTEXT-FREE (T NIL) :STRIPPED-P T)
i.e. the malleated block is ACCEPTED by the :context-free-only arm and connect-block (src/validation/block.lisp:2554-2566) stores its body unconditionally.

REFUTED PARTS. (1) Block weight is NOT deferred: src/validation/block.lisp:1652-1655 runs calculate-block-weight > +max-block-weight+ -> :block-too-heavy inside %check-block, i.e. in the context-free arm, ahead of the :context-free-only return. One of the four listed rules is simply wrong. (2) "Cheap unmetered work for a peer" is false for the finality/BIP34 cases: %check-block calls validate-block-header with PoW enabled (block.lisp:1594-1605), so a stored side-branch block must carry real proof-of-work at the fork's difficulty. (3) "Re-validated on every reorg attempt" is bounded: :non-final-tx and :bad-coinbase-height are both in *deterministic-invalid-block-errors* (block.lisp:2999-3007), so the first reorg attempt poisons the block and its whole subtree :invalid (block.lisp:3262 %mark-block-subtree-invalid) and protocol.lisp:993-1007's duplicate-invalid / bad-prevblk gates then refuse re-offers. (4) The witness-verdict-stays-transient choice is documented and reasoned at block.lisp:2953-2996 (witness bytes are not hash-committed, so poisoning would wedge a recoverable block), and perform-reorg self-heals witness-STRIPPED stored bodies by forgetting them for re-download (block.lisp:3499-3514); the same guard block-witness-stripped-p is applied at the two activate-block store sites (block.lisp:3942, 4103) and in process-received-block (ibd.lisp:3634-3640).

RESIDUAL (why not fully refuted): the accept-downloaded-block/connect-block relay path has no witness guard at all, and a witness mutation on a NON-coinbase tx (:bad-witness-merkle-match) is caught by neither block-witness-stripped-p nor the deterministic allowlist, so a witness-mutated side-branch body -- free to produce, the block hash is unchanged -- lands on disk where Core refuses it at admission. I traced (but did not execute) that such a body would fail every reorg through block.lisp:3223-3266 and fall into retry-best-reorg-candidate's `t' branch (ibd.lisp:3586-3593), the documented "ONLY permanent-reject path", against a completable best chain. That is a real hardening gap, but the finding as filed rests on the two claims refuted above, so S3.

s2.title_prefix: testmempoolaccept validates each transaction in isolation; Cor
s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION. Built the standard P2SH(OP_TRUE) fixture, a parent spending the funding UTXO and a child spending the parent, and called the handler directly:
  (bl.rpc::rpc-testmempoolaccept node (list (list parent-hex child-hex)))
=> parent: ("allowed" . T) ("vsize" . 85) fees base 1.0d-4, effective-includes #(<parent wtxid>)
   child:  ("allowed" . YASON:FALSE) ("reject-reason" . "missing-inputs")
Core for the same batch takes ProcessNewPackage (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/mempool.cpp:343-346, txns.size() > 1) -> AcceptMultipleTransactionsAndCleanup with ATMPArgs::PackageTestAccept (validation.cpp:1815-1817, 498-513), which calls IsWellFormedPackage first (validation.cpp:1436) and m_viewmempool.PackageAddTransaction(ws.m_ptx) after each member's PreChecks (validation.cpp:1473), so the child's in-package input resolves and it is not "missing-inputs". Our handler (src/rpc/mempool.lisp:504-615) has no package branch at all -- it is a flat (dolist (tx decoded ...)) over bl.val:validate-transaction-for-mempool; grep for "package" in src/rpc/mempool.lisp finds only the batch-count cap (line 519-523) and submitpackage, so the behaviour is not handled elsewhere. bl.val:validate-package-for-mempool does exist (src/validation/packages.lisp:549) but it MUTATES the mempool and has no test_accept mode, so "the machinery already exists next door" is optimistic.

TWO DETAILS IN THE FINDING ARE WRONG, and they narrow the headline example. PackageTestAccept passes package_feerates=false (validation.cpp:509-513), so (a) effective-feerate/effective-includes stay per-transaction, not package-level (validation.cpp:1295-1297, 1542-1544) -- Core does NOT report "the package effective-feerate" or list both wtxids -- and (b) CheckFeeRate is still applied per member (validation.cpp:945: !bypass_limits && !m_package_feerates), so a genuine 0-fee CPFP parent fails Core's testmempoolaccept with min-relay-fee-not-met and the child comes back "validation unfinished", not allowed:true. The divergence therefore bites on any multi-tx batch whose members each pay their own way (we say missing-inputs, Core says allowed) and, for true CPFP, on the shape/reason of the answer rather than a flat allowed flip.

The rest of the claim holds as read: no package-error field, no reject-details field, and no allow_replacement=false handling anywhere in the handler. Severity stays S2 -- a wrong dry-run verdict that a wallet or LN implementation can gate broadcast on, no consensus or in-node relay effect.

s2.title_prefix: invalidateblock reorgs only to the invalidated block's parent an
s2.evidence:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION. src/validation/block.lisp:3772-3807 `invalidate-block` does one `perform-reorg` tip->parent, marks the subtree :invalid, returns; no `activate-best-chain`. Grep of the whole tree: `activate-best-chain` has exactly two callers, src/networking/ibd.lisp:2224 and src/node/init.lisp:1103 — none in validation/*.lisp or rpc/*.lisp. src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:761-791 `%chain-control-block` only takes the node lock and funcalls the op. Core refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp:1695-1713 does `ActiveChainstate().InvalidateBlock(...)` then `if (state.IsValid()) ActivateBestChain(state)` inside the RPC helper. RAN (scripts/dev.sh eval, rc=0): built A1..A3 as the active chain plus a fully-downloaded valid fork B1..B2 with chain-work = work(A2)+1, then invalidated A3 ->
(:OK T :REASON NIL :TIP-BEFORE "c0030000" :TIP-AFTER-INVALIDATE "c0020000" :HEIGHT-AFTER 2 :A2 "c0020000" :B2 "d0020000" :BEST-VALID-TIP-STILL-AVAILABLE "d0020000" :TIP-AFTER-EXPLICIT-ABC ("d0020000" 2))
i.e. the RPC leaves the node on the parent while `best-valid-tip` already names the heavier downloaded branch, and an explicit `activate-best-chain` immediately switches to it. So the wrong tip is DETERMINISTIC right after the call, not merely a race — Core's own test/functional/rpc_invalidateblock.py:53-57 (`invalidateblock(badhash); assert_equal(getblockcount(), 4); assert_equal(getbestblockhash(), besthash_n0)`) would read height 1 on our node. No comment or test documents this as deliberate: tests/validation/reorg-tests.lisp:470-500 only invalidates on a single chain with no competitor.
CONSEQUENCE PARTLY OVERSTATED: the finding's last clause ("on a node whose sync thread is not running that pass (e.g. -connect=0 with peers present), the switch may not happen at all") is REFUTED. src/node/init.lisp:1120-1158 `%sync-thread-loop` calls `%sync-pass` (>=1 peer) -> sync-blockchain -> start-ibd -> run-ibd, which activates at ibd.lisp:2222-2235, and with ZERO peers it calls `%sync-offline-activation` (init.lisp:1083-1117), which calls `activate-best-chain` directly every <=5 s. The idle wait also exits early after +behind-retry-seconds+ = 5 (src/node/peers.lisp:722, init.lisp:1028) when the header tip is above our height, which is exactly the post-invalidate state. So recovery is bounded at ~5-30 s, not never. Severity stays S2 on the strength of the deterministic broken synchronous contract (wrong tip/height, rewound UTXO+mempool for that window), not on a permanent stall.

s2.title_prefix: getblocktemplate returns a cached template verbatim — curtime, b
s2.evidence:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION. src/rpc/mining.lisp:330-336: `(cached (%gbt-cached-result node tip-hex txs-updated))` then `(when cached (return-from rpc-getblocktemplate cached))` — the stored alist is returned verbatim; :338-354 shows the validity test is `(or (= cached-updated txs-updated) (<= (- now built-at) +gbt-cache-seconds+))` with +gbt-cache-seconds+ = 5 (:204), so an unchanged mempool counter keeps it alive with no age bound. curtime/bits/target are frozen at build time (%gbt-assemble :364-397 reads them off the template; src/mining/assembler.lisp:243-252 computes curtime = (max now mintime) and bits = (next-block-required-bits tip curtime) once). Core refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/mining.cpp:884-888 applies `UpdateTime(&block, consensusParams, pindexPrev)` AFTER the cache decision on every call, and node/miner.cpp:49-64 recomputes `pblock->nBits = GetNextWorkRequired(...)` when fPowAllowMinDifficultyBlocks; the reply's target (:939) and curtime/bits (:1013-1014) come from that refreshed block. RAN (rc=0) both halves:
(:POW-LIMIT-BITS "1D00FFFF" :BITS-AT-GAP-1100 "1C00FFFF" :BITS-AT-GAP-1300 "1D00FFFF" :CACHE-HIT-SAME-TXCOUNTER-AGE-100000S (("bits" . "1C00FFFF") ("curtime" . 1788247527) ("target" . :FROZEN)) :CACHE-HIT-CHANGED-TXCOUNTER-OLD NIL)
— on :testnet4 `next-block-required-bits` flips 1C00FFFF -> 1D00FFFF purely on the 1200 s gap, and `%gbt-cached-result` handed back the frozen alist after 100,000 s of simulated age. getmininginfo's "next" does recompute per call (src/rpc/mining.lisp:448-453), so the two RPCs really can disagree.
CONSEQUENCE NARROWER THAN FILED, hence S3 not S2: (1) regtest is unaffected in substance — get-expected-bits returns the prev block's bits for :regtest before any min-difficulty branch (src/validation/block.lisp:489-493), and in Core regtest powLimit == every block's nBits, so UpdateTime's recompute is a no-op there; mainnet/signet never change bits with time, so they only see a stale `curtime`, which is harmless ("time" is mutable and mintime is tip-derived, so the stale value is still > MTP). (2) On testnet3/4 the stale window closes at the first mempool update plus 5 s (the `or` arm above), so it persists only on a node with a genuinely quiet mempool; a longpolling miner is woken by exactly that mempool change and then gets a rebuild. Within that window the two consequences are real as stated: the served target is the pre-20-minute (hard) one, and a miner that rolls nTime past tip+1200 while keeping the served bits builds a header our own validate-difficulty rejects as :bad-difficulty (src/validation/block.lisp:545-562 requires powLimit exactly once the gap exceeds +testnet-min-difficulty-spacing+ = 1200).

s2.title_prefix: Pruning is not a flush trigger, so block files below tip-288 ar
s2.evidence:
MECHANISM (read, both trees). Ours: src/validation/block.lisp:2709-2720 — `(bl:maybe-periodic-flush chain-state)` then, unconditionally, `(when (bl:automatic-pruning-p) (bl.store:prune-old-blocks ...))`. maybe-periodic-flush (src/node/flush.lisp:329-361) fires ONLY on `*blocks-since-flush* >= +flush-every-n-blocks+` (25000, flush.lisp:3), `>= +flush-every-n-seconds+` (600, flush.lisp:12), or the coins-cache size trigger. prune-old-blocks (src/storage/blocks.lisp:841-932) contains no flush call of any kind (`grep -n flush src/storage/blocks.lisp` → only flat-file-flush at :125, a blk-file write flush), and the only prune-lock producers are the INDEXES (src/node/indexes.lisp:309,355 via bl.store:register-prune-lock) — nothing holds the prune horizon at the last durably-flushed coins height. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:2751-2755 sets fFlushForPrune when the prune set is non-empty, :2766 folds it into `should_write`, and :2795-2800 UnlinkPrunedFiles runs inside the same FlushStateToDisk that then does `CoinsTip().Flush()/Sync()` at :2812 — so Core cannot unlink a file whose coins are not already durable. Claim about both trees is accurate.

CONSEQUENCE (EXECUTED, warm image). Positive control — recovery works when the bodies are on disk: built a 6-block fixture chain, dropped the coinbase coins of heights 2-6 (coins durable only through h=1), then `(bitcoin-lisp::recover-inconsistent-chainstate node cs)` → `(:TIP-HEIGHT 6 :RECOVERY-WITH-BLOCKS T :REWOUND-TO 1)`. Pruned variant — same setup, bodies of heights 1-4 removed from the block-store index (get-block then returns NIL, src/storage/blocks.lisp:427-489): `(:TIP-HEIGHT 6 :BLOCK1-BODY-ON-DISK NIL :BLOCK6-BODY-ON-DISK T :RECOVERY-RESULT NIL :HEIGHT-AFTER 6)`. NIL is the abort: src/node/recovery.lisp:180-182 logs "no committed ancestor found on disk (blocks pruned below the UTXO tip?); resync required" and src/node/init.lisp:669-674 turns it into `init-error "chainstate inconsistent and unrecoverable: move ~A aside and re-sync"`. Ordering matters and is as filed: the block-body walk runs at init.lisp:669, while the cheap coins-DB-pointer reconciliation that needs no bodies (reconcile-coins-db-best-block) only runs later at init.lisp:812, so it never gets the chance to rescue this case.

CORRECTIONS TO THE WRITE-UP (do not change the verdict): (a) the deleted range is bounded by the prune TARGET, not literally tip-288 — prune-old-blocks deletes oldest-first only until total-bytes <= target, so the kept window is max(288, target/avg-block) blocks; the failure needs flush-gap > kept window, which is an IBD/catch-up phenomenon (600 s of pruned IBD is thousands of blocks) and not a steady-state one (post-IBD the 600 s timer fires roughly per block). (b) it also needs the crash to land while the 3-phase marker is set (src/node/flush.lisp:243-277), i.e. during a flush or after a failed one. (c) the second impact (pruned-height > best-height stalling further pruning via the `(when (<= min-keep-height start) (return 0))` guard at blocks.lisp:882-883) is real arithmetic but is mostly unreachable in the same run, since the large-gap case aborts at (b) instead; recovery.lisp:172-174 states the assumption the finding attacks ("pruning ... lags the tip by the whole block window, so it is far below this rewind point") — true only while the flush gap is small. Net: real Core divergence, reachable consequence = full resync of a pruned node after a crash-during-flush. S2 stands (not S1: needs a crash window, no consensus impact).

s2.title_prefix: Re-mined transactions are never removed from the reorg disconne
s2.evidence:
MECHANISM (read). Core: refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:3105-3106 in ConnectTip runs BOTH `m_mempool->removeForBlock(block_to_connect->vtx, ...)` AND `disconnectpool.removeForBlock(block_to_connect->vtx)`, so a re-mined tx is gone from the disconnect pool before MaybeUpdateMempoolForReorg (:294-322) can hit its `removeRecursive` arm. Ours: %reorg-disconnect pushes every non-coinbase tx of every disconnected block (src/validation/block.lisp:3146-3161); the ONLY other references to reorg-disconnected-block-txs in the whole tree are the trim at :3158-3159 and the consume at :3395 (`grep -n "disconnected-block-txs" src/validation/block.lisp` → 3082, 3130, 3155, 3158-3161, 3395) — nothing removes re-mined txs. The connected loop at :3361-3364 calls only bl.mp:mempool-remove-for-block, which touches the mempool, not the pool list. readd-disconnected-txs-to-mempool (block.lisp:2885-2906) then does: validate → if `(not (mempool-has ... txid))` → `(bl.mp:mempool-remove-spenders mempool txid n-outputs)`, and mempool-remove-spenders (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1794-1807) calls mempool-remove-recursive on every in-pool spender.

EXECUTED (warm image, no files modified). Scenario: P re-mined by the new chain (its input removed from the UTXO set, its output P:0 added as a confirmed UTXO), child C spending P:0 sitting in the mempool, then `(bitcoin-lisp.validation::readd-disconnected-txs-to-mempool mempool (list p) utxo 200 cs)` →
  (:CHILD-IN-POOL-BEFORE T :PARENT-READDED NIL :CHILD-IN-POOL-AFTER NIL)
Negative control, identical fixture with the re-mined parent removed from the list (exactly what Core's disconnectpool.removeForBlock achieves) →
  (:CHILD-IN-POOL-BEFORE T :PARENT-READDED NIL :CHILD-IN-POOL-AFTER T)
So the eviction is caused by the re-mined parent remaining in the disconnect pool, and the child of a CONFIRMED parent is wrongly removed with its descendants (reason :reorg, so it is not re-added or re-relayed). Consequence is as filed — mempool/relay damage after any reorg that re-mines a tx with an unconfirmed CPFP/chained child; no consensus effect. S2 stands.

s2.title_prefix: REORG-DISCONNECTED-BLOCKS retains every disconnected block in full
s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED (mechanism read-traced, magnitude measured).

(1) The retention is real and unbounded. src/validation/block.lisp:3162-3164, inside %reorg-disconnect's per-entry loop: `(push (cons block (bl.store:block-index-entry-height entry)) (reorg-disconnected-blocks r))` sits INSIDE `(when block ...)` but OUTSIDE the `(when mempool ...)` that feeds the capped pool, so it runs for every disconnected block on every reorg. `grep -n reorg-disconnected-blocks -r src/` gives exactly one writer (3163) and two readers (3323 PHASE C wallet/ZMQ/index notifications, 3406 a log line) — nothing ever trims it, and nothing bounds the loop length.

(2) The 20 MB cap is inert for memory, as claimed. trim-disconnect-pool (block.lisp:18-37) pops entries off reorg-disconnected-block-txs only; those entries hold `(rest (bl.ser:bitcoin-block-transactions block))` (block.lisp:3143) — the block's OWN transaction list, still reachable through the (BLOCK . HEIGHT) pair pushed two forms later. Dropping the tx list frees nothing while the block is retained. The cap does still bound PHASE C's mempool re-add work; it does not bound memory, which is what its own comment (block.lisp:3131-3137, "Unbounded, a deep reorg over full blocks pins hundreds of MB") and Core's MAX_DISCONNECTED_TX_POOL_BYTES exist for.

(3) Core diverges exactly as stated. refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:3597-3614: InvalidateBlock's `while (true)` loop constructs a FRESH `DisconnectedBlockTransactions disconnectpool{MAX_DISCONNECTED_TX_POOL_BYTES}` per iteration and calls `LimitValidationInterfaceQueue(...)` at the top of each iteration ("Make sure the queue of validation callbacks doesn't grow unboundedly"); DisconnectTip's shared_ptr<CBlock> dies with the iteration. Nothing accumulates block bodies across the loop.

(4) No depth bound exists on our disconnect side. invalidate-block (block.lisp:3771-3805) makes ONE perform-reorg call tip -> parent; +activation-step-blocks+ (block.lisp:3641) bounds only activate-best-chain's CONNECT-side target via %activation-step-target, never the tip->fork disconnect. The RPC (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:760-790, %chain-control-block) adds no depth guard. Pruning's fork-below-pruned-height refusal (block.lisp:3452-3457) is the only refusal, and only when pruning is on.

(5) Magnitude, MEASURED in the warm image: a synthetic 2,401-tx block serialized to 897,772 bytes conses 2,928,768 bytes when deserialized via br-read-bitcoin-block -> ratio 3.26x (`(:SERIALIZED-BYTES 897772 :TXS 2401 :BYTES-CONSED-DESERIALIZING 2928768 :RATIO 3.2622626)`). At ~1.5 MB mainnet blocks that is ~5 MB retained per disconnected block, so the finding's "10k-block invalidateblock retains 10+ GB" is if anything conservative (~50 GB).

Severity: S2 stands — a real unbounded-memory divergence, but reachable only through a deep rollback (operator invalidateblock at an old hash, or a deep more-work fork), not through ordinary block flow.

s2.title_prefix: A fork block failing with a non-allowlisted error is neither poisoned
s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED — reproduced end to end in the warm image.

EXECUTED (scripts/dev.sh eval, test-support fixtures, no files changed): built chain A (genesis->A1->A2, active) and chain B (genesis->B1->B2 stored) then B3 with a timestamp <= its MTP so %reorg-connect's header-time-too-old-p pre-check (block.lisp:3222-3225) returns the non-allowlisted :time-too-old. Output:
  (:TIP-AFTER-A 2) (:TIP-AFTER-B2 2)
  (:CONNECT-BLOCK-REORG-OUTCOME (NIL :TIME-TOO-OLD))
  (:TIP-AFTER-B3 2 :BEST-PREFIX (160 2)) (:B3-STATUS :VALID)
  (:BEST-VALID-TIP-HEIGHT 3 :BEST-VALID-TIP-PREFIX (176 3))
  (:PASS 0 :SWITCHED NIL :DETAIL :TIME-TOO-OLD :TIP 2 :B3-STATUS :VALID)
  (:PASS 1 :SWITCHED NIL :DETAIL :TIME-TOO-OLD :TIP 2 :B3-STATUS :VALID)
  (:PASS 2 :SWITCHED NIL :DETAIL :TIME-TOO-OLD :TIP 2 :B3-STATUS :VALID)
  (:PASS 3 :SWITCHED NIL :DETAIL :TIME-TOO-OLD :TIP 2 :B3-STATUS :VALID)
So after the failed reorg the fork tip is NOT poisoned (:VALID, not :invalid), best-valid-tip still names it (height 3, hash prefix B0 03), and activate-best-chain re-runs the full disconnect-to-fork / connect / roll-back cycle and fails identically on every pass, with the tip pinned at 2. That is the claimed infinite retry, executed.

Mechanism, read-traced:
- block.lisp:3262 poisons only when %deterministic-consensus-failure-p is true. Eval: (%deterministic-consensus-failure-p :script-failed) => NIL, :bad-merkle-root => NIL, :too-many-sigops => NIL, :missing-input => T; the allowlist is exactly the 8 keywords at 3004-3013.
- best-valid-tip (block.lisp:3613-3641) filters on chain-work > min-work, status /= :invalid, and block-exists-p only — a :valid/:header-valid entry with a body on disk is re-selected forever.
- activate-best-chain's failure arm (block.lisp:3766-3770) stores the keyword in MISSING and `(return)`s out of the dotimes, so no second candidate is tried in that pass either.
- run-ibd calls activate-best-chain unconditionally every sync pass (src/networking/ibd.lisp:2222-2231).
- The section comment's mitigation at block.lisp:2994 ("soft-rejected (retry-best-reorg-candidate's bounded rejected-set)") is indeed inapplicable: rejected-reorg-candidates lives only in src/networking/ibd.lisp (3324, 3329-3336, 3421) and is read only by %best-completable-reorg-target; validation cannot see it at all (bl.net depends on validation, not the reverse).

Core side verified: InvalidBlockFound (refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:1985-1994) sets BLOCK_FAILED_VALID and erases from setBlockIndexCandidates for every result except BLOCK_MUTATED (called from ConnectTip at :3074); FindMostWorkChain's fFailedChain walk (:3170-3196) strips the whole doomed branch; ActivateBestChain nulls pindexMostWork on fInvalidFound (:3423-3425). Core therefore always makes progress.

One correction to the impact text, not enough to move severity: the "a genuinely valid competing branch is never activated" half is PARTIALLY mitigated on a live node — retry-best-reorg-candidate's catch-all arm (ibd.lisp:3585-3596) does %reject-reorg-candidate on any unrecognized error, so a second-best branch that is in that bounded candidate set can still activate through that driver. What is not mitigated at all is the per-pass futile reorg by activate-best-chain, which is the expensive half (full disconnect to the fork point + revalidation + rollback, every ~30 s, forever). Severity S2 unchanged: liveness/resource wedge, not a consensus split.

((BITCOIN-LISP:ZMQ-NOTIFY-BLOCK-CONNECTED (BITCOIN-LISP.VALIDATION:CONNECT-BLOCK))

s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED by execution. `scripts/dev.sh eval` over bip30-enforced-p per network (src/validation/block.lisp:1222-1232) returned:
((:MAINNET 227931 ((0 T)(1 T)(100 T)(227930 T)(227931 NIL)(227932 NIL)(1983701 NIL)(1983702 T)))
 (:TESTNET3 21111 (... (227930 NIL) ...))
 (:TESTNET4 1 ((0 T)(1 NIL)(2 NIL)(3 NIL)(100 NIL) ... (1983702 T)))
 (:SIGNET 1 (same as testnet4)) (:REGTEST 1 (same as testnet4)))
And with feature_block.py's own config: (apply-test-activation-heights '("bip34@2")) on :regtest gave (:BIP34-HEIGHT 2 :BIP30-AT-1 T :BIP30-AT-2 NIL :BIP30-AT-120 NIL).

On mainnet the ancestor is null while pprev->nHeight < 227931, so Core enforces at 227931 inclusive while we stop at 227930 — a real one-block-early divergence (inert: no duplicate txid there). No compensating check exists elsewhere: src/validation/block.lisp:1708-1714 is the only BIP30 site, and apply-block-to-utxo-set overwrites silently (src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:564-573 passes :allow-overwrite for coinbase outputs; the utxo-set arm at :787-793 just setf's the entry). The docstring calls this a deliberate approximation 'omitting only the extra enforcement Core applies on a non-canonical fork past the BIP 34 height' — that reasoning is factually wrong for the three null-BIP34Hash chains, so it does not excuse the divergence.
CONSEQUENCE, judged separately: directly reachable on regtest and exercised by Core's own oracle — test/functional/feature_block.py:93-94 runs with -testactivationheight=bip34@2, plants DUPLICATE_COINBASE_SCRIPT_SIG (b'\x01\x78' = height 120) in the height-1 coinbase (:113-118, legal for us too since validate-coinbase-height returns T below activation, src/validation/block.lisp:1298-1300), and at :853-861 asserts Core rejects the byte-identical coinbase at height 120 with 'bad-txns-BIP30' ('BIP30 is always checked on regtest, regardless of the BIP34 activation height'). Our eval shows bip30-enforced-p 120 = NIL under that exact config, so we accept the block and overwrite the still-unspent duplicated coinbase coin (CVE-2012-1909). The impact statement is OVERSTATED for live chains, though: on testnet4/signet BIP34Height is fixed at 1 and -testactivationheight is regtest-gated in both trees (Core chainparams.cpp:44-67 ReadRegTestArgs; ours src/node/init.lisp:187-190 config-errors off regtest), so every coinbase from height 1 up carries a distinct height prefix and no duplicate txid can be constructed there — the missing check is unreachable defense-in-depth on those networks, and mainnet's off-by-one at 227931 is historically inert. So: real consensus-rule bug, demonstrably reachable only in a supported test configuration (where it silently accepts a block Core rejects and breaks the functional-test oracle) — S2 stands rather than S1.

"df6696e2...d979") ("fee" . 8.58d-6) with :R2-IN-MEMPOOL NIL and :R1-STILL-IN-MEMPOOL T — i.e. post-restart the wallet builds a second replacement priced against the ORIGINAL's fee, the mempool rejects it (it under-pays R1), and the wallet is left holding a third unbroadcastable tx while the original's marker now points at it. Confirmed.
(1) safeTx hold — RAN: in the state where the original is still in the mempool, listunspent(0, 9999999) on the original's change output returns (vout 1, 48.99999285, "safe" YASON:FALSE) with the marker and (vout 1, 48.99999285, "safe" T) after clearing it. So wallet-coins.lisp:274-280 does drop Core's spend.cpp:390-399 hold and default (only-safe) coin selection will fund from a replaced tx. NUANCE: this needs the original to still be in the mempool — in the ordinary case where the replacement was accepted, the original is evicted and the earlier depth-0/not-in-mempool gate (wallet-coins.lisp:270-272, Core's same rule) skips the coin anyway; and "can never confirm" is overstated (in the reachable state it is the REPLACEMENT that is stuck, the original can still confirm). Mechanism and the safe-flag flip are exactly as filed, so I leave S2 rather than upgrading; the (1) narrative is a shade stronger than the reachable case.

s2.title_prefix: bumpfee forces fOverrideFeeRate, skipping the mempool-min-fee an
s2.evidence:
CONFIRMED, and reproduced end-to-end.

Core reading verified: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/feebumper.cpp:288-292 runs CheckFeeRate (:60-115: mempoolMinFee, minTotalFee, GetRequiredFee, maxtxfee) on the user-supplied feerate and never touches fOverrideFeeRate; `grep -rn fOverrideFeeRate refs/bitcoin/src` gives only fees.cpp:41 (the read), rpc/spend.cpp:225 (behind override_min_fee) and rpc/spend.cpp:570 — and bumpfee's own option parsing is rpc/spend.cpp:1071, `SetFeeEstimateMode(..., /*override_min_fee=*/false)`. So bumpfee never overrides in Core.

Ours: src/wallet/psbt.lisp:1780-1783 sets (wcc-override-feerate cc) t in BOTH branches; src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:339-342 then returns early, and only the minTotalFee clause is ported (psbt.lisp:1796-1810, old_fee + +incremental-relay-fee-rate+ 100 sat/kvB over the new vsize). Small correction to the write-up: Core's GetMinimumFeeRate applies the mempool-min floor only in the ESTIMATE branch (fees.cpp:101-106), so the override early-return itself skips only the GetRequiredFeeRate floor; the mempool-min enforcement Core loses is the one in feebumper::CheckFeeRate, which we simply do not port. Net divergence as filed.

RAN (regtest fixture): original sent at 5 sat/vB, then set the pool's rolling minimum to 50000 sat/kvB and called bumpfee with fee_rate 20:
  (:EFFECTIVE-MIN-FEE-SAT-KVB 50000
   :BUMPFEE-RESULT (("txid" . "34d2866c...485b") ("origfee" . 7.15d-6) ("fee" . 2.86d-5) ("errors" . #()))
   :REPLACEMENT-IN-MEMPOOL NIL :ORIGINAL-IN-MEMPOOL T
   :REPLACEMENT-IN-WALLET T
   :ORIGINAL-MARKED-REPLACED "34d2866c...485b")
bumpfee reports success with an empty errors array; our own mempool refuses the tx (src/validation/transaction.lisp:1248-1254 returns :insufficient-fee against mempool-effective-min-fee-rate), the broadcast failure is only logged (wallet-spend.lisp:2450-2468, %wallet-commit-transaction), yet the replacement is in the wallet and the original is marked replaced. Core returns feebumper::WALLET_ERROR from CheckFeeRate before any of that. IMPACT NUANCE: "funds stuck until abandontransaction" is a little strong — the original stays in the mempool and can still confirm, after which the phantom replacement becomes conflicted; the solid consequence is a false success, a wallet-held unbroadcastable tx, and wrong coin availability/balance in the meantime (the original's change also reads safe=false because of the bogus marker). Wallet-level, recoverable: S2 stands.
